title: Forget LLM: MIT's New RLM (Phase Shift in AI)
summary: Discover AI walkthrough of MIT's Recursive Language Model (RLM) inference paradigm. Addresses 'context rot' — degradation of LLM reasoning as context length grows, especially on dense scientific/financial/medical tasks. RLM uses Python-function recursion (LLM_query) to spawn temporal-isolated copies of the model handling subtasks at reduced complexity, aggregates results. Transforms pure-memory problem into management problem. Positioned as third element of an early-2026 architecture trio: Google's meta-controller transformer + DeepSeek's topological residual-stream optimization + MIT's RLM inference layer (all three compatible).
claims: Context rot: LLM reasoning capability degrades non-linearly with context length, especially on information-dense tasks (science, finance, medicine)
RLM (MIT) is an inference-time technique, not a new architecture — compatible with existing LLMs
Recursive LLM_query Python function spawns temporally-isolated subtask handlers at reduced complexity, aggregates results
Transforms pure-memory problem into management problem (context-window-as-stack vs context-window-as-flat-buffer)
Compatible-stack framing: Google meta-controller transformer + DeepSeek topological optimization + MIT RLM = three orthogonal optimizations of early 2026, combinable
